subject: chemistry
title: Bond energies
key_idea: Breaking bonds takes in energy and making bonds releases energy. The overall energy change is the energy needed to break bonds minus the energy released making bonds. A negative result means the reaction is exothermic.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) This section covers where the energy change in a reaction comes from.

items.meaning: The energy needed to break one mole of a particular covalent bond, in kJ/mol. The same amount is released when that bond forms.

items: Energy must be supplied to **break bonds** in the reactants. Breaking bonds is endothermic.
Energy is released when bonds in the products are formed. **Making bonds** is exothermic.
In an exothermic reaction, the energy released forming new bonds is greater than the energy needed to break existing bonds.
In an endothermic reaction, the energy needed to break existing bonds is greater than the energy released forming new bonds.
Bond breaking takes in energy. Bond making gives out energy.
Exothermic: more energy is given out than taken in. Endothermic: less is given out than taken in.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) Add up the bond energies for the bonds broken and the bonds made, then find the difference.

blocks.label: Overall energy change
blocks.formula: energy change = energy to break bonds − energy released making bonds
where: energy to break bonds is the sum of the bond energies of the reactants, in kJ/mol
energy released making bonds is the sum of the bond energies of the products, in kJ/mol

items: Use the balanced equation. Multiply each bond energy by the number of those bonds.
A negative answer means the reaction is exothermic. A positive answer means it is endothermic.

blocks.text: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl. Bond energies: H–H = 436, Cl–Cl = 243 and H–Cl = 432 kJ/mol.

items.text: The sign is negative, so the reaction is exothermic.

checks.q: (AQA: Higher tier) Explain why a reaction is exothermic in terms of bond breaking and bond making.
checks.a: Energy is needed to break bonds and energy is released when bonds form. More energy is released making bonds than is needed to break bonds.

checks.q: (AQA: Higher tier) In a reaction, the bonds broken need 1000 kJ/mol and the bonds made release 1300 kJ/mol. Calculate the overall energy change and state the type of reaction.
(AQA: Higher tier) Why must you multiply a bond energy by a number in a calculation?
checks.a: The balanced equation can have more than one of that bond, such as 2 H–Cl bonds in 2HCl.

worked_example.question:
The equation shows the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide:

2 H–O–O–H → 2 H–O–H + O=O

Bond dissociation energies in kJ per mole: O–O = 138, O=O = 496, O–H = 463.

Calculate the overall energy change for the reaction.
answer_points: Energy change = bonds broken − bonds made = 2128 − 2348 = −220 kJ.
worked_example.tip: An answer of −220 kJ scores all three marks. A mistake in one step does not stop the later marks.

worked_example.question:
In some chemical reactions, bonds are broken in the reactant molecules and new bonds are formed to make the product molecules.

Hydrogen reacts with fluorine.

H₂ + F₂ → 2HF

The bond energies are:
H–H = 436 kJ/mol
F–F = 158 kJ/mol
H–F = 562 kJ/mol

Calculate the energy change for this reaction.
answer_points: = −530 kJ/mol (the negative sign shows an exothermic reaction).
worked_example.tip: One mark each. The last mark is for the correct sign or for stating exothermic.

worked_example.question:
Two students investigate the burning of methane in oxygen.

Methane + Oxygen → Carbon dioxide + Water

Bond energies in kJ/mol: O–H = 459, C=O = 799, O=O = 494. The C–H bond energy is not given.

The reaction is exothermic and 802 kJ of energy are given out when 1 mole of methane burns.

Student A thinks the C–H bond energy is 432 kJ/mol. Student B thinks it is 411 kJ/mol.

Who is correct?

Use the bond energies and the energy given out in the reaction to calculate the C–H bond energy.
answer_points: Equation: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Bonds made: 2 × C=O and 4 × O–H.
Energy released making new bonds = (2 × 799) + (4 × 459) = 3434 kJ.
Energy needed to break bonds = 3434 − 802 = 2632 kJ.
C–H = 1644 ÷ 4 = 411 kJ/mol, so Student B is correct.
worked_example.tip: Three marks: bonds made, bonds broken, then the C–H value. Divide by 4 because there are four C–H bonds. The answer alone scores 0 without working.
